answer:
In promptfoo, you can cap concurrency with the `-j` (or `--max-concurrency`) flag on `eval`. I believe the default is 4, but check the docs for your version.

```powershell
npx promptfoo eval -j 2
```

You can also set it in your config file (`promptfooconfig.yaml`):

```yaml
evaluateOptions:
  maxConcurrency: 2
```

If you're hitting provider rate limits rather than just wanting fewer parallel requests, I believe `evaluateOptions` also accepts a `delay` setting that pauses between requests. I'm less certain of its exact name and units, so confirm it in the promptfoo docs.

I don't know of a per-provider concurrency setting in promptfoo, so I can't confirm whether one exists. If you need different limits for different providers, check the provider configuration docs or the current CLI help (`npx promptfoo eval --help`).
